original_question: In the generic 3-dimensional time-optimal control problem q˙ = f(q) + u g(q), |u| <= 1, is every individual time-optimal trajectory forced to have only finitely many switching points, even if one does not assume a uniform neighborhood-wise bound on the number of switchings?
target_in_paper: Section I.A, “Singularities of time-optimal trajectories,” specifically the weaker open question stated after the definition of sw(q): “We also do not know if a weaker property, the finiteness of the number of switching points for any individual time-optimal trajectory is valid.” This is posed for the generic 3-dimensional case, after the stronger local question whether sw(q)<∞ for every q∈M. (p. 2). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right mathematical target: the generic 3-dimensional single-input time-optimal setting q̇=f(q)+ug(q), |u|≤1, and the weaker question about finiteness of switching points for each individual optimal trajectory, rather than the stronger neighborhood-wise bound encoded by sw(q). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
missing_details: The paper assumes that f and g are smooth (C∞) vector fields. (Section I, p. 1). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The state space is a 3-dimensional manifold M, with q∈M; the question is not stated only in Euclidean coordinates. (Section I, pp. 1–2). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
The time-optimal problem is posed with fixed endpoint. (Section I, p. 1). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

Admissible controls are measurable functions u with |u|≤1, and admissible trajectories are Lipschitz curves in M. (Section I, p. 1). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

A switching point is explicitly defined as a point where the admissible trajectory is not smooth. (Section I.A, p. 2). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The nearby stronger local question is formulated via sw(q): the minimal k such that every time-optimal trajectory contained in a sufficiently small neighborhood of q has at most k switching points; sw(q)=∞ if every neighborhood of q contains a time-optimal trajectory with infinitely many switching points. (Section I.A, p. 2). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The paper explicitly separates your target question from the stronger one sw(q)<∞ for all q∈M, so that contrast should be stated explicitly if you want full paper-faithfulness. (Section I.A, p. 2). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

The intended scope is Part I.A (generic smooth pair), not Part I.B (real-analytic, not necessarily generic systems). (Section I, pp. 1–2). ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
refined_question: Let M be a 3-dimensional manifold, and let f,g be a generic pair of smooth (C∞) vector fields on M. Consider the fixed-endpoint time-optimal control system q̇=f(q)+u g(q), |u|≤1, where admissible controls u are measurable and admissible trajectories are Lipschitz. Is it true that every individual time-optimal trajectory has only finitely many switching points, where a switching point is a point at which the trajectory is not smooth? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))
justification: Section I sets up exactly the control system q̇=f(q)+ug(q), |u|≤1, on an n-dimensional manifold M, with fixed endpoint, measurable controls, and Lipschitz admissible trajectories (p. 1). In Part I.A, Agrachev specializes to the generic case, notes that for n=3 the stronger local boundedness problem is open, defines sw(q), and then states the weaker question that your draft is aiming at: whether any individual time-optimal trajectory has finitely many switching points (p. 2). He immediately adds that, among the questions in that section, the one on generic 3-dimensional systems is in his view the most interesting. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7063141/some-open-problems---sissa-people-personal-home-pages))

citations.label: Problem setup for time-optimal trajectories: q̇=f(q)+ug(q), |u|≤1; fixed endpoint; measurable controls; Lipschitz trajectories
Definition of switching point and of sw(q); stronger local question sw(q)<∞ for all q∈M
Exact weaker open question on finiteness of switching points for any individual time-optimal trajectory
Author’s remark that the most interesting question is the one on generic 3-dimensional systems
